name: Container Orchestration System
oneLineDescription: A simplified Kubernetes-inspired container orchestration system for learning and demonstration purposes.
whatItIs: A Go-based container orchestration system that manages containerized workloads across a cluster of worker nodes. It implements core Kubernetes concepts including a control plane with state store, scheduler, and controller manager; a node agent daemon that manages local containers via Docker; a REST API for external interaction; a gRPC API for agent-control plane communication; and a kubectl-style CLI tool. The system supports automated deployment, manual scaling, and basic self-healing (automatic rescheduling on node failure). It is explicitly a learning and demonstration system — not a production Kubernetes replacement — implementing simplified versions of core orchestration concepts.

coreUserFlows: An operator creates a workload via CLI, which the control plane schedules onto available worker nodes and the agents start as containers.
An operator scales a workload via CLI, and the controller manager reconciles by scheduling additional instances or terminating excess ones.
A worker node stops sending heartbeats, the node health controller marks it offline, and all its instances are automatically rescheduled onto healthy nodes.
An operator retrieves logs for a workload via CLI, which the REST API proxies from the relevant node agents.
outOfScope: ConfigMaps, Secrets, or environment variable injection
DNS-based service discovery or Service abstraction
Namespaces — system uses a single flat namespace
Resource enforcement via cgroups — resource requests tracked only
Multi-container pods, DaemonSets, StatefulSets, and Jobs
Log aggregation or historical log storage

Stores the state of each running container instance, linking it to its parent workload and assigned node.

crossCuttingPrinciples: All state mutations flow exclusively through the Control Plane API — no component accesses the state store directly from outside the control plane.
The store.Store interface is injected into all components; the etcd implementation satisfies this interface, enabling substitution.
No authentication or authorization is implemented anywhere in the system — it is explicitly out of scope.
Structured logging via go.uber.org/zap is used throughout; a *zap.Logger is passed as a constructor argument to all components.
The scheduler is deterministic: given the same node and workload inputs, it always produces the same placement decision.
The node agent executes instructions only and never makes scheduling decisions — all scheduling logic lives in the control plane.
Controller loops run on a configurable interval (default 10 seconds) and process workloads independently so one failing workload cannot block others.
Domain types store.Node, store.Workload, and store.Instance defined in internal/store/store.go are the canonical types used across all components.
Optimistic concurrency control via a version field is used in the state store to detect concurrent modification conflicts.
specSummary: The Container Orchestration System is a Go-based learning and demonstration project that implements simplified versions of core Kubernetes orchestration concepts. It manages containerized workloads across a cluster of worker nodes using a control plane / data plane split. The control plane consists of four components: an etcd-backed cluster state store (Feature 1), a gRPC+REST API server (Feature 5), a filter-then-score scheduler (Feature 3), and a controller manager running replica and node-health reconciliation loops (Feature 4). Each worker node runs a node agent daemon (Feature 2) that registers with the control plane, pulls and manages containers via the local Docker Engine, sends periodic heartbeats, and reports status changes over gRPC. A Cobra-based CLI tool (Feature 7) provides kubectl-style commands for operators, communicating exclusively over REST. An optional overlay networking layer (Feature 6) using VXLAN tunnels and Linux bridges enables cross-node container communication. The system is built in phases: state store first, then control plane API and scheduler in parallel, then node agent, then controller manager, then CLI, and finally networking. Key constraints include: no authentication anywhere, no persistent volumes, no rolling updates, no service discovery, no namespaces, single control plane node, Docker Hub images only, and resource requests tracked but not cgroup-enforced. All domain types are defined in internal/store/store.go, all components receive a store.Store interface via constructor injection, and structured logging via zap is used throughout.
